key_insight: Patients at highest risk of training-data membership inference largely remained the same across tested models, enabling early screening with four small models.
clinical_relevance: Screening before production-model training could help clinical AI teams identify privacy risks that cohort-average metrics may hide.
method: Measured patient-level vulnerability to membership inference attacks.
Compared risk rankings across training recipes, architectures and initializations.
Developed a four-model screening tool and assessed protection without removing flagged records.
evidence_signal: The study evaluated 7,789 models across six clinical datasets and four modalities, including two adapted pretrained medical models; stronger weight decay reduced the exposed cohort by up to threefold.
watch_item: Screening flags potential vulnerability rather than guaranteeing privacy, and its reliability beyond the tested datasets and configurations remains uncertain.
paper_title: Automated screening of privacy risks in medical AI
